findings.title: SourcePattern::matches allocates one Vec<bool> per pattern token per name
findings.claim: `matches` allocates a fresh `next` vector inside the per-token loop and is invoked once per directory child per pattern component during COPY selection, so a pattern of N tokens costs N+1 heap allocations for every candidate filename on a hot path.
findings.suggested_fix: Allocate both buffers once outside the token loop and swap them each iteration (clearing the scratch buffer), so a match costs at most two allocations regardless of token count.

findings.title: Every scute layer is read and SHA-256 hashed at least twice per build
findings.claim: `verify_references` hashes every manifest layer in full (src/cache/resolve.rs:105 -> Cache::copy_verified, src/cache/mod.rs:129-138), then `verify_chain` immediately re-opens and re-hashes the same scute blobs through `CheckedBlob` (src/cache/chain.rs:142-144), and `VerifiedScute::prepare` reads them a third time to emit the verity tree (src/cache/chain/prepared.rs:52), so the largest immutable artifacts in the system are streamed and hashed 2-3 times back to back.

let receipts = cache.verify_references(&image)?;
            let chain = cache.verify_chain(&image)?;
findings.suggested_fix: Have `verify_references` skip the layers that `verify_chain` will authenticate anyway (or have `verify_chain` consume the receipts already produced), so each scute blob is content-hashed exactly once per build.

findings.title: Compressed scutes are fully decompressed twice just to learn their length
findings.claim: `verify_scute` runs a complete zstd decode of a compressed scute into `io::sink()` only to measure the decoded byte count, then reopens the blob and decodes it a second time to compute the verity root, doubling both the read and the decompression cost for every compressed layer.
findings.suggested_fix: When `descriptor.annotations.data_blocks` is present the geometry is already known, so stream once and compute the trailing padding at EOF instead of running a separate measuring pass.

findings.title: Verity hashing reads cache blobs and writes the tree through unbuffered Files
findings.claim: The uncompressed hot path hands a raw `File` straight to `ScuteExtent::format` for both input and hash-tree output (and `DecodedBlob::Plain` is likewise unwrapped, while only the compressed variant gets a `BufReader` at src/cache/chain.rs:204), so every read/write issued by the block-oriented verity formatter becomes its own syscall rather than being batched.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the data source in a `BufReader` and the hash scratch in a `BufWriter` sized to a multiple of the 4096-byte block (e.g. 64 KiB) on this path, as the compressed path already does.

findings.title: COPY re-resolves and re-opens every path prefix once per descendant file
findings.claim: For each descendant entry the destination writer calls `resolve` on the full joined path, which issues an `openat2`+`fstat` per path component from the root (src/copy/destination.rs:111-151), and `leaf` then calls `directory` which re-walks and `mkdirat`/`openat2`s the same prefix again (src/copy/destination.rs:152-180, :242), making a directory copy O(entries x depth) syscalls over directories that were already created and stat'd moments earlier.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the already-opened parent directory descriptor down the walk (the entries arrive in sorted order, so each new path shares a prefix with the previous one) instead of re-resolving from the root for every entry.

findings.title: descendants() scans the entire captured context and repeats a map lookup per entry
findings.claim: `descendants` iterates every entry in the whole `BTreeMap` context rather than the ordered range under `self.resolved`, and re-evaluates the loop-invariant `self.is_directory()` — itself a `BTreeMap` lookup keyed by `PathBuf` — once per entry, so copying one small subdirectory from a large repository costs a full scan plus one map lookup per repository entry, repeated for every selected source.
findings.suggested_fix: Hoist the `is_directory()` check out of the closure and use `BTreeMap::range` over the `self.resolved` prefix so the walk is proportional to the subtree, not the whole context.

findings.title: Wildcard source selection scans every context key for each candidate path
findings.claim: Each wildcard path component enumerates children by scanning the full key set and comparing `p.parent()`, so the cost is O(candidates x total entries) per component on an ordered map that already supports a prefix range query.
findings.evidence_quote:
for child in self
                            .entries
                            .keys()
                            .filter(|p| p.parent() == Some(actual.as_path()))
findings.suggested_fix: Use `BTreeMap::range` bounded by the `actual` prefix to enumerate direct children instead of filtering the whole key set.

findings.title: Unbounded zstd decode when a scute omits its data-blocks annotation
findings.claim: When `descriptor.annotations.data_blocks` is absent the measuring pass decompresses the layer with no length limit at all, so a compression-bomb scute (zstd is listed as untrusted input) costs unbounded CPU and wall time here, and the measured size is then used to materialize a scratch file of that size in `prepare` (src/cache/chain/prepared.rs:59-83), turning it into workspace exhaustion — this is a denial-of-service vector, not merely a slow path.
findings.evidence_quote: io::copy(&mut source, &mut io::sink())?
findings.suggested_fix: Apply an absolute decoded-size ceiling (e.g. the same `FilesystemSize::LOGICAL_DEVICE_BYTES` bound used elsewhere) to the unannotated branch so no layer can decode without a limit.

findings.title: Command output relay flushes a write syscall per output line
findings.claim: `io::stdout()`/`io::stderr()` are unconditionally line-buffered in Rust (unlike C, this holds even when redirected to a file or pipe), so relaying a verbose command's output costs at least one `write` syscall and one lock acquisition per newline for the whole duration of every RUN step.
findings.suggested_fix: Relay into a block-buffered writer over the inherited stdout/stderr descriptors (flushing at relay completion) rather than through the line-buffered `Stdout`/`Stderr` handles.

findings.title: Named owner lookup resolves, opens and parses /etc/passwd twice
findings.claim: Resolving a named owner calls `account` once for the uid field and again for the gid field, and each call re-resolves the path, re-opens the file, re-reads up to 16 MiB and re-scans every line to find the same record.
findings.evidence_quote:
Some(name) => (
                self.account("/etc/passwd", name, 2)?,
                self.account("/etc/passwd", name, 3)?,
            ),
findings.suggested_fix: Return both fields from a single `account` read of the matching line instead of reading and parsing the database twice.

findings.title: Glob matcher heap-allocates a state vector per token per candidate name
findings.claim: `matches` allocates one `Vec<bool>` up front and another inside the per-token loop, and it is invoked once per candidate child during wildcard selection (src/copy/source.rs:119-121), so matching costs tokens x candidates heap allocations rather than reusing two scratch buffers.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep two reusable buffers (clearing and resizing in place, swapping them each token) so the matcher allocates at most once per call.

findings.title: argv slicing panics when the process is exec'd with empty argv
findings.claim: `&arguments[1..]` panics with a slice-index-out-of-range if `std::env::args_os()` yields zero elements, which Linux permits via execve with an empty argv array.
findings.evidence_quote:
let arguments: Vec<_> = std::env::args_os().collect();
    match HelperInvocation::parse(&arguments[1..]) {
findings.suggested_fix: Use `arguments.get(1..).unwrap_or_default()` (or match on an empty argv explicitly and return a diagnostic failure) instead of unchecked slicing.

findings.title: BuildError::Execution(String) flattens every stage failure into a string
findings.claim: All three stage coordinators funnel richly typed failures through `BuildError::Execution(error.to_string())`, so the resulting error has no `source()` chain and the caller cannot distinguish a failed untrusted RUN command from a host storage/namespace failure.
findings.evidence_quote:
#[error("build execution: {0}")]
    Execution(String),
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the concrete failure (or at minimum a `#[source]`-annotated boxed error plus a discriminant separating command-outcome failures from host failures) instead of a formatted String.

findings.title: InventoryError conflates malformed untrusted CBOR with host I/O failure
findings.claim: `InventoryError` is a single opaque `String` newtype, so `Inventory::decode` on attacker-controlled CBOR and `Builder::current`'s failure to read `/proc/self/exe` produce indistinguishable error values with no source chain and no preserved `io::ErrorKind`.
findings.suggested_fix: Split InventoryError into at least `Invalid(&'static str)` / `Decode(#[source] ...)` for untrusted-input failures and `Io(#[from] io::Error)` for host failures.

findings.title: Symbolic COPY mode AST is publicly re-exported but entirely unused
findings.claim: `Change`, `Clause`, `Operator`, `Permission` and `Permissions` plus their accessors (`who()`, `changes()`, `operator()`, `permissions()`) are public, yet the only consumer anywhere in src/ or tests/ is the private `CopyMode::apply`, so the parser's internal representation is accidental public API.
findings.evidence_quote: pub use mode::{Change, Clause, CopyMode, ModeError, Operator, Permission, Permissions};
findings.suggested_fix: Re-export only `CopyMode` and `ModeError`, keeping the clause/change/permission representation private to the `mode` module.

findings.title: FilesystemSize validation only reachable by formatting a u64 back into a string
findings.claim: `FilesystemSize` exposes no numeric constructor, so validating a decoded inventory's `size_bytes` against untrusted CBOR requires the `format!("{}B", n).parse()` round-trip, which also mislabels any failure through `ValueError`'s text-syntax variants.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `impl TryFrom<u64> for FilesystemSize` carrying the same capacity/alignment checks and have both `FromStr` and the inventory validator call it.

findings.title: StorageExecutionFailure Display dumps the whole cleanup state via {:?}
findings.claim: The `#[error]` format embeds `{cleanup:?}`, so the user-facing message for a failed command renders the Debug of a retained `TeardownFailure`/finalized volume, and the type provides no `source()` for programmatic inspection.
findings.suggested_fix: Render only the cleanup's `FailureDiagnostics` (already available via `cleanup_error()`) in Display and implement `source()` to return the primary outcome.

findings.title: CommandTimeout::from_str makes parsing depend on the current clock
findings.claim: `FromStr` samples `Instant::now()` to reject durations that cannot form a deadline, so parsing the same recipe text is not a pure function of the input and the check is stale by the time the timeout is actually used.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the parsed duration against a fixed maximum constant during parsing and perform the `checked_add` at deadline-construction time where the failure is actionable.

findings.title: Parser errors stringified instead of chained as sources
findings.claim: `TransformError::Dtb`, `CacheError::Manifest` (src/cache/resolve.rs:144) and `ContextError::Git` (src/context/mod.rs:36) all store `error.to_string()`, discarding the underlying typed error so `source()` returns None and callers cannot inspect the specific devtree/pichi-artifact/gix failure.

findings.suggested_fix: Hold the concrete error types as `#[from]`/`#[source]` fields rather than their formatted text.

findings.title: unreachable!() in the public network cleanup path
findings.claim: `cleanup` returns early for `Pending::Complete` at line 97 and then re-matches the same value with an `unreachable!()` arm, so the invariant is enforced only by the earlier `matches!` rather than by the type.

findings.suggested_fix: Restructure as a single `match self.pending` whose `Pending::Complete` arm returns `Ok(())`, eliminating the panicking arm.

findings.title: zstd scute measuring pass is unbounded when data-blocks is absent
findings.claim: A lock-pinned image whose manifest omits `dev.pichi.scute.verity.data-blocks` on a ScuteZstd layer reaches a fully uncapped `io::copy` over an attacker-supplied zstd stream, and when the annotation is present the derived cap is never cross-checked against any policy maximum for compressed layers.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an absent `data_blocks` on a compressed scute as invalid, and intersect the declared value with a policy constant such as `FilesystemSize::LOGICAL_DEVICE_BYTES` before using it as the `take()` limit.

findings.title: Decoded compressed extent is written to build tmpfs at an attacker-chosen size
findings.claim: Because `extent.size()` for a compressed layer is derived from the unbounded measuring pass in security-001, a malicious pinned image can drive this `io::copy` to write an arbitrarily large decoded extent into the RAM-backed build workspace before any size policy is consulted.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject `extent.size()` above the supported logical device capacity before materializing, so the tmpfs write is bounded by policy rather than by the manifest.

findings.title: Private /proc masking omits kernel info-leak entries the design asks to restrict
findings.claim: The fresh procfs handed to the untrusted command read-only-remounts only `sys`, `sysrq-trigger`, `irq` and `bus`, leaving `/proc/kallsyms`, `/proc/sched_debug`, `/proc/timer_list`, `/proc/keys`, `/proc/latency_stats` and `/proc/interrupts` readable, which is narrower than SANDBOX-DESIGN.txt 7.3's requirement to restrict process inspection and than standard container practice.
findings.evidence_quote: for path in ["sys", "sysrq-trigger", "irq", "bus"] {
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the masked set to cover the kernel-address/scheduler/keyring info-leak entries (overmounting them with an empty read-only node rather than only remounting read-only).

findings.title: splice/tee/vmsplice allowed in the command filter without a stated need
findings.claim: The otherwise strict default-deny allowlist grants `splice`, `tee` and `vmsplice` to the untrusted command, a pipe-buffer attack surface with a repeated history of kernel LPE (vmsplice CVE-2008-0600, splice/Dirty Pipe CVE-2022-0847) and no evident requirement for a filesystem-population workload.
findings.evidence_quote:
sys::__NR_splice,
            sys::__NR_tee,
            sys::__NR_vmsplice,
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `vmsplice` (and `tee`, and `splice` if package tooling does not require it) from the allowlist, or record the concrete workload that needs each one.

findings.title: Formatter helper execs mke2fs as full initial-namespace root under chroot only
findings.claim: The Formatter role unshares mount/net/IPC/UTS but not CLONE_NEWUSER, and execs the formatter without `CommandPrivileges::apply`, `no_new_privs` or any seccomp filter, so a defect in the trusted formatter is confined only by an escapable `chroot` (src/formatter/input.rs:134-136) while holding every capability in the initial user namespace.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the bounding set to the capabilities mke2fs actually needs and set `no_new_privs` before `exec`, and prefer `pivot_root` over `chroot` for the formatter root as is already done for command roots.

findings.title: StagedDirectory::publish is public with no verification gate in the type
findings.claim: SANDBOX-DESIGN.txt 11.3 requires staging, identity verification, then atomic publication, but the verification step lives only in `AssembledImage::publish_inventory`, so a library consumer can call `StagedDirectory::create` -> `store_blob` -> `publish` and atomically publish a never-verified artifact directory.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `publish` `pub(crate)` or require a verification receipt token produced by `AssembledImage`, so the publication contract is enforced by the type system at this layer too.

findings.title: prctl allowlist includes PR_CAP_AMBIENT, partly undoing the ambient-set clear
findings.claim: Option 47 is `PR_CAP_AMBIENT`, so the untrusted command can re-raise granted capabilities into the ambient set that `CommandPrivileges::finalize` deliberately cleared and verified empty, making them survive exec of otherwise unprivileged image binaries; this is bounded by the permitted set and so is not an escalation, but it weakens a stated invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove option 47 from the prctl allowlist unless a qualified distro workload is shown to need ambient-capability inheritance, and document the decision alongside the ambient-set verification in privileges.rs.

findings.title: SPECULATIVE: fixed-offset slice on re-encoded DTB relies on an out-of-crate invariant
findings.claim: SPECULATIVE: `output[24..32]` and `bytes[24..32]` index attacker-influenced DTB buffers at fixed offsets and are safe only because `devtree::Tree::parse` rejects blobs under 40 bytes and `OwnedTree::encode` always emits a 40-byte header — invariants held entirely in a separate crate, so a dependency change would turn this into a supervisor panic on image-supplied input.
findings.evidence_quote: output[24..32].copy_from_slice(&bytes[24..32]);
findings.suggested_fix: Use checked `get(24..32)` on both buffers and return `TransformError::Dtb` on `None` so the safety condition is local to this crate.

findings.title: Formatter runtime order validated as String but produced in Path order
findings.claim: The producer emits runtime files in `BTreeMap<RelativePath<FilePath>, _>` order (Rust `Path`/`PathBuf` `Ord` compares component-by-component) while `Formatter::validate` re-checks the ordering on the serialized `String` paths (byte-lexicographic), so a legitimate runtime set such as {"usr/lib/a", "usr/lib-x"} is emitted in Path order ("usr/lib/a" < "usr/lib-x" because component "lib" < "lib-x") but rejected by the string check ("usr/lib/a" > "usr/lib-x" because '/' 0x2F > '-' 0x2D); the validator should compare the same key the producer sorts on, i.e. compare `Path::new(&w[0].path) >= Path::new(&w[1].path)` (or have `CapturedFormatter` key its map on the UTF-8 string).
findings.evidence_quote: || self.runtime.windows(2).any(|w| w[0].path >= w[1].path)
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the two orderings with one key — either validate with `Path::new(&w[0].path) >= Path::new(&w[1].path)`, or sort/store the captured formatter runtime by its UTF-8 string path so emission and validation agree.

findings.title: EnteredRoot::execute doc says "No CARAPACE support yet" but CARAPACE is supplied
findings.claim: The rustdoc on the command-execution entry point states the documented `$CARAPACE` build variable is unimplemented, while the step layer in fact injects it into every command script, so a reader auditing the build-variable contract is told the opposite of what the code does.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the stale "No CARAPACE support yet" sentence and state that CARAPACE reaches the shell as an `export` prefix prepended to the script by the caller, not through `Command::env`.

findings.title: Crate root says pipeline assembly and publication are unimplemented
findings.claim: The crate-level `//!` summary — the first thing any reader of this lib sees — claims full pipeline assembly and publication are still pending, but `Pipeline::run` already selects a bootstrap/firmware/carapace/inherited path, assembles the OCI layout and publishes it atomically.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the crate-root summary to describe the implemented pipeline (input capture, storage assembly, isolated execution, sealing, OCI+inventory publication) and name only the genuinely absent stage (`platform`) as unimplemented.

findings.title: Step's seven-state machine never documents which transitions exist or their order
findings.claim: `Step` is the central lifecycle typestate (Ready, Running, Cancelling, Reaping, Draining, Quiescent, Finishing) but neither the type doc, the module doc, nor the state markers state the legal transition order; only three negative `compile_fail` examples hint at it, and the one place in the repo that does spell an order out (ARCHITECTURE.md) names states that no longer exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a transition diagram to the `Step` rustdoc (and a one-line order to `LabelPolicy` and `Supervision`) naming each consuming method and its source/target state, and correct the stale state names in ARCHITECTURE.md.

findings.title: Volume doc omits that Drop performs a lazy MNT_DETACH unmount
findings.claim: Every comparable RAII owner in this crate documents its destructor's behaviour in rustdoc, but `Volume<Mounted>`'s doc says nothing about Drop even though dropping one silently performs a lazy `MNT_DETACH` unmount — the exact operation SANDBOX-DESIGN 10.4 forbids treating as clean finalization — with the only explanation in a non-doc `//` comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Drop sentence to the `Volume` rustdoc stating that abandonment attempts a lazy detach as a best-effort fallback, never flushes, and never yields an `Unmounted` value, so only `unmount()` constitutes clean finalization.

findings.title: ChildReaper doc describes Drop behaviour but ChildReaper has no Drop impl
findings.claim: The `ChildReaper` doc asserts what its destructor deliberately does, but no `impl Drop for ChildReaper` exists anywhere in src/, so a reader auditing teardown ordering may search for a destructor that is not there or assume a guard exists where there is none.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to "This owner has no destructor: `PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER` stays set for the process lifetime, because clearing it cannot clean up already-adopted children."

findings.title: PrivateMountNamespace doc omits that Drop restores the original namespace
findings.claim: The public `PrivateMountNamespace` doc describes creation constraints but never says that dropping the guard calls `setns` back to the original mount namespace, while the only sentence in the file that mentions Drop says the opposite — it sits on the private `commit()` method, where the claim is true only after the restoration handle has been taken.
findings.suggested_fix: State on the public `PrivateMountNamespace` type that Drop performs a best-effort `setns` back to the original namespace (diagnosing but not propagating failure) unless the guard has been committed by `CommandRoot::enter`.
